It is a standard protective fluoride coating and is chemically simple.

This tests a new cation family (Zr) rather than the P, B, or F/Cl anion chemistries that all gave S/Cl/P-containing gas or halide products.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV) insulator with no electronic leakage path, and its phosphate chemistry is closely related to the PS4 units in Li6PS5Cl, so it should form a chemically compatible, low-reactivity interlayer. It is also a common interface coating for oxide cathodes, and its P(V) framework should resist oxidation at 4.0 V vs Li.

LiF is a wide-gap insulator with very high anodic stability, so it should not oxidize at 4.0 V vs Li. Its F- anion is hard and poorly reducible, so it should have little driving force to react with the sulfide framework of Li6PS5Cl, unlike the phosphate interlayer whose P(V) and S/Cl contact produced SO2/SCl4/P2O5 products. It is a standard protective fluoride coating and is chemically simple.
